Stated Claim / Post Context:
Trump is slammed for staying silent for hours on nationwide ground stop crisis… before saying it 'could' have been caused by 'old broken stuff'

The FAA grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon, citing 'extraordinary circumstances for safety reasons' and upending thousands of travelers' weekend plans.

Actual Article Body:
By WILKO MARTÍNEZ-CACHERO, US REPORTER

Published:  11:01 AEDT, 14 November 2026   |  Updated:  15:29 AEDT, 14 November 2026

President Donald Trump was blasted for not addressing the Federal Aviation Administration's rare ground stop of all flights nationwide on Friday for hours before saying it 'could' have been caused by 'old broken stuff.'

The FAA had grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon, citing 'extraordinary circumstances for safety reasons' and upending thousands of travelers's weekend plans before the ground stop was lifted shortly before 8.30pm ET.

The reason for the halting of US flights was initially communicated by the Air Traffic Control System Command Center (ATCSCC) at 3.54pm ET.

Around 5.52pm ET, Trump posted on Truth Social about his desire to 'make our entertainment industry great again,' outlining how he was working with politicians across both aisles on the Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act but not making any mention of the ground stop.

CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins highlighted Trump's post and wrote on X: 'Trump posts, not about the ground stop, but about reviving the entertainment industry in bipartisan fashion.'

Trump's weekend schedule amid the aviation crisis listed Executive Time at 8am on Saturday and Sunday, with no other scheduled engagements.

The President said the ground stop did not seem to be a cyber attack and that it could be a result of an old system that 'relies on some old broken stuff' he had tried to upgrade, according to FOX News correspondent Peter Doocy.

Trump is getting constant updates on the situation, the Daily Mail understands.

President Donald Trump posted 'about his desire to 'make our entertainment industry great again' as the FAA ground stop continued on Friday afternoon

The flight halt was the first since January 11, 2023, which happened after a key FAA computer system malfunctioned

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of any threats to the US, adding that the incident was a 'communication outage' and rejecting comparisons to the aftermath of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

'This isn't the same comparison to 9/11,' Mullin told reporters outside the White House on Friday. 'That's a road I won't go down.'

At a press conference later on Friday, Mullin said the introduction of some new technology into an old air traffic control system overwhelmed it.
